summary: Full backend + frontend testing of NEW KPI Strip feature on Panoramica. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests pass (auth guard, 24h/7d/30d structure, invalid period fallback, 9-key order, opened.series (24 buckets) sum==value, alerts.breakdown, alerts.value vs DB, opened 7d vs DB, availability sub vs /overview/clients, snapshot->trend activation with fake docs cleaned up). Frontend: kpi-strip renders with all 9 tiles (availability=66.7%, clients=1, alerts=1655, opened=119, mttr=8.9h shown in hours as required for >=120min, noise=32.7%, backup=1, hw=0, agents=38). Period selector (24h/7d/30d) persists in localStorage 'kpi_period' after reload. Tile navigation works: alerts -> /alerts?status=active, availability -> /network-status, clients -> /clients. Search-client + filter-all/problems/ok present below strip; ClientStatusTable renders. Mobile viewport 390px correctly hides desktop strip (MobileDashboard active). No console errors, no runtime overlay. Regression: /api/overview/clients returns 200; /alerts page loads.
critical_code_review_comments: KpiStrip.js: MTTR & noise tiles have series=[] from backend, so Sparkline always renders empty <div class='h-7'/> placeholder — intentional per playbook (flow KPIs), but consider a small histogram of opened alerts for consistency to avoid visual gaps.

routes/kpi.py: _current_state() computes agents_total/agents_offline mixing managed_agents + connectors; this is fine but the sub 'su {agents_total}' semantically conflates two heterogeneous populations — consider splitting into 2 tiles or clarifying the sub label.
routes/kpi.py: db.alerts.find() loops ~1655 docs twice (state + flow); acceptable at current scale but a $facet aggregation would be more efficient at 10k+ alerts.
KpiStrip.js: axios call has no auth header — relies on axios global default set elsewhere; verified working in test but worth documenting.
test_credentials: admin info@86bit.it via TOTP (as provided) — worked first try
seed_data_creation: Inserted 2 fake kpi_snapshots docs (marked _test_iter145=True) inside test_record_kpi_snapshot_enables_trend and deleted them in finally block. No residual test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: KPI strip feature works end-to-end. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_kpi_strip_iter145.py can be re-run as regression. Note: pytest requires pyotp (installed). Data in preview: 1655 active alerts, availability 66.7% (2/3 vitals online), 38 agents offline (all).
